articles.title: 京东 1 号会员店 10 月 28 日起调整会员权益：尊享卡返 2% 赠金，每月权益需消费解锁
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，京东旗下 1 号会员店宣布将于 10 月 28 日起调整会员权益体系。根据官方公告，此次调整的核心变化是购物返利从“满 200 元返券”改为按订单金额比例返还“赠金”，尊享卡会员返 2%、普通卡会员返 1%，每月赠金上限分别为 500 元和 200 元。1 元赠金可抵扣 1 元人民币，特殊商品不参与返金也不支持赠金抵扣。新老用户按续费渠道和时效分流。10 月 28 日前已开通、且未在 1 号会员店 App 内续费的老用户，会籍期内继续享受原满 200 返券权益；会籍过期 30 天内在 App 内续费的，可在旧权益与新返金权益之间二选一；过期超过 30 天再续费，或 10 月 28 日后新购卡的用户，适用新规则。通过京东 PLUS 等其他渠道续费的，权益以卡面及商品详情页宣传为准。另外，1 号店“每月尊享权益”的规则也一并改写。新规下，权益从“满 49 元消费后兑换鸡蛋或牛奶”变为每月在 10 元无门槛补贴金、2 张 6 元运费券或其他商品中任选其一，每月可领取 1 次。首月免消费门槛，此后在当前会籍期内累计实付每满 19 元，解锁一次领取资格。公告同时注明，新权益自 10 月 28 日后逐步开放，暂未看到的用户需等待推送。健康与生活类权益同步扩充。尊享会员新增 2 次在线问诊、1 次陪诊和 1 次绿通挂号；车险、养车、家政保洁、家电清洗等场景提供专属折扣。这两类权益计划于 10 月 28 日起陆续上线，具体以会员中心展示为准。实际上，2026 年以来，1 号会员店已多次改动会员规则：此前“每月尊享权益”的领取门槛从自付 6 元运费即可单领鸡蛋，逐步变为需单笔订单实付满 49 元。IT之家注：1 号会员店前身为 1 号店，2020 年由京东转型为付费会员制精选超市，主打线上会员店模式，依托京东供应链和物流履约，核心城市多数商品可实现半日达或次日达。尊享年卡官方定价 198 元，普通年卡 99 元。

articles.title: ATK RS8 Air / Neo 电竞键盘发布：87 配列，到手价 299 元起

articles.title: Meta AI 负责人罗希特 · 帕特尔离职创业，打造微软 Office 替代方案 Ndoc
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，据科技媒体 TechCrunch 今天报道，Meta 人工智能负责人罗希特 · 帕特尔（Rohit Patel）已经离开公司，他曾在 Meta 从事 AI 研发工作八年，并担任 Meta 超级智能实验室负责人。据报道，帕特尔已创立 Ndoc 公司，他将开发一款原生 AI 办公软件，旨在取代微软 Office 和谷歌 Workspace。这名前 Meta 研究员希望，Ndoc 不能只是叠加在现有工作流的 AI 工具，而是要改变人们使用各种工具的碎片化现状。例如大家经常要来回切换 Excel、Word、PowerPoint 和 Tableau 等软件，还要不断把内容复制粘贴到 ChatGPT 中。Ndoc 的目标是将上述所有工作流整合到统一空间之中，让所有人都能轻松办公。据悉，Ndoc 在同一界面中整合了三个主要模块。「Stage」用于展示关键内容，如幻灯片、仪表盘、模拟结果和迷你应用；「Narrative」用于呈现分析内容、带编号的引用、生成图表，以及解释数据背后原因；「Model」则用于存放底层数据集和 Python 脚本。在实际使用中，用户可以上传数据集让 Ndoc 分析，并根据结果撰写说明性文本。这款软件更远大的目标是“重新定义文件”，其文档可导出为独立的“.ndoc.html”文件，然后在所有浏览器打开。帕特尔希望将这种格式开源，让其他开发者也能使用。帕特尔是近期离开 Meta 的众多高管和研究员之一。此前，Meta 全球事务负责人乔尔 · 卡普兰（Joel Kaplan）、AI 研究员安德鲁 · 塔洛克（IT之家注：Andrew Tulloch），以及负责工作场景 AI 产品的负责人艾米莉 · 道尔顿 · 史密斯（Emily Dalton Smith）均已离职。

articles.title: 《三角洲行动》协助警方破获游戏史最大 DMA 外挂案，涉案金额超 2000 万
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，《三角洲行动》官方今日宣布，在《三角洲行动》安全团队协助下，广东警方成功侦破“Foah”特大 DMA 外挂案，累计抓获犯罪嫌疑人 16 名，涉案金额超过 2000 万元。核心外挂作者、销售总代理均被抓获，多个分代理发卡平台、外挂陪玩工作室已被捣毁。目前，案件正在审查起诉。IT之家从官方公告获悉，2025 年下半年，一款名为“Foah”外挂线索出现在《三角洲行动》安全团队的视野内，团队迅速行动部署线上打击、处罚作弊账号，并收集资料和信息，积极配合警方推进侦办，追溯源头线索。同年 10 月，多个销售外挂、使用外挂牟利的嫌犯被捕。一个数千人的 DMA 外挂频道听闻风声，宣布解散，并试图换皮继续非法经营转移视线。但新群很快关停，管理员留下一句：“换壳失败了”。同年 11 月，该外挂核心嫌犯发出最后公告 ——“由于某些不可抗力，FO 将永远不会回归。”主要嫌疑人具备反侦察意识，通过境外软件联络，并通过虚拟货币结算。但警方持续深挖，逐步厘清外挂陪玩工作室、发卡平台、分代理、总代理、幕后作者五个层级的关系网，并锁定了核心作者和多个嫌疑人。信息确认后，广东警方在山东、河南、江西等地展开收网行动，至今年 5 月，陆续抓捕了包括：外挂原作者、总代理、分代理、工作室牟利等 16 名嫌疑人，全案涉案金额超 2000 万元。至此，游戏史上最大涉案金额的 DMA 外挂，正式终结，案件进入审理和判决。

articles.title: The AI Boom Will Pull Back, Warns Former SEC Chair Gary Gensler
articles.content: Former SEC Chair Gary Gensler says history suggests today’s AI investment boom will not continue indefinitely. He's expecting some form of slowdown or reversal within the next 18 to 30 months, and says mounting debt could determine how disruptive that correction becomes. Gensler also weighs in on interest rates, monetary policy, financial stability, and the possibility that the U.S. has overbuilt AI infrastructure. Gensler, now Professor of the Practice of Global Economics and Management at MIT's Sloan School of Management, speaks with Bloomberg Surveillance hosts Tom Keene and Paul Sweeney. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: 消息称上汽奥迪暂未停产四环标油车，对售出车型终身兜底
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，10 月 26 日，奥迪中国宣布已分别与合作伙伴签署战略协议，四环标和字母标正式“分家”，引发外界关注。据蓝鲸新闻今日报道，知情人士透露，上汽奥迪旗下仍有 Q6、A7L、A5L Sportback 三款四环标油车在售，且均暂未停产。但新的四环品牌产品，未来上汽奥迪将不再销售。至于售后，该知情人士透露，上汽奥迪将对售出的四环车型终身兜底，但后续消费者也可根据自己的意愿去一汽奥迪修。另有知情人士向记者透露，上汽奥迪的 A5L Sportback 后续移交一汽奥迪销售已差不多定下来，但预计什么时间点现在还没有最终确定。“很多细节都还在谈，包括哪个车型纳入一汽奥迪生产，哪个车型先放上汽奥迪那儿生产，然后一汽奥迪销售，这些信息时间节点都在谈。”其也向记者证实，目前售后确实也是南北奥迪在谈的方向，包括上汽奥迪四环标车型售后何时接入一汽奥迪，“以 A5L Sportback 为例，目前售后有些备件是这款车独有的，那这些备件信息，包括用户信息等，后续都要接入一汽奥迪系统，不过这些对接和协同还在谈细节。”据IT之家此前报道，奥迪中国 10 月 26 日宣布，奥迪分别与合作伙伴签署了战略协议，旨在强化奥迪四环品牌与 AUDI (奥迪字母标) 品牌之间的差异化定位及各自的战略侧重，并进一步明确“双品牌、双合作伙伴”渠道架构。根据此前公告，在四环品牌方面，奥迪和中国一汽将持续强化多元且均衡的豪华产品矩阵，涵盖豪华新能源车型以及下一代智能燃油车型，其中包括奥迪 A6L e-tron、Q6L e-tron 以及全新奥迪 A5L、A6L 等。奥迪和上汽集团将进一步深化 AUDI (奥迪字母标) 品牌的发展，致力引领中国豪华智能网联新能源汽车市场。继 2025 年奥迪 E5 Sportback 成功推出后，首款 SUV 奥迪 E7X 已于今年 5 月上市，并取得亮眼的市场关注和用户反响。随着专属 AUDI (奥迪字母标) 品牌的奥迪创新技术中心在上海的正式落成。此外，各项客户服务、售后保障及经销商业务均将继续平稳有序开展。上汽奥迪在 2027 年底前仍可正常销售四环产品。上汽奥迪旗下四环品牌产品以及全新 AUDI (奥迪字母标) 品牌产品的售后服务，均将保持平稳运营。

articles.title: 艺卓推出全新 DuraVision 系列显示器，专为触控笔输入优化
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，艺卓今日宣布推出全新 DuraVision 系列触控显示器，分别为 21.5 英寸的 FDF2182WT-AS、18.5 英寸的 FDF1983WT-AS 和 15.6 英寸的 FDF1683WT-AS。IT之家了解到，这三款显示器专为触控笔输入优化，用户可直接在屏幕上书写、批注、签名和绘图，将传统纸笔写字体验带入数字化环境。机内附赠的主动式触控笔支持 4096 级压感，可带来自然书写体验，并具备悬停功能，可在触控笔接触屏幕前显示光标位置。同时，该系列显示器最多支持 10 点触控，并支持捏合、旋转、拖动和滑动等多点触控手势，用户可以根据不同任务的需要，在手指触控和触控笔输入之间自由切换。FDF2182WT-AS 还带有 LaidBack 支架，可灵活调整屏幕倾斜角度，获取更加舒适的写字姿势。此外，该系列产品专为办公室、医疗机构、制造工厂和公共服务系统等场景打造，官方提供 3 年质保。

articles.title: Anthropic 确认其内部系统遭访问：客户对话、模型权重未受影响
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，据《华盛顿邮报》当地时间 10 月 26 日报道，网络安全初创公司 Cathedral 称，其研究人员利用 AI 智能体在不到 12 小时内通过第三方商业软件的漏洞，找到进入 Anthropic 内部系统的路径。Anthropic 随后确认，部分销售、人力资源和 IT 系统遭到访问，但客户与 Claude 的对话、模型回复、源代码及模型权重均未受到影响。Cathedral 由美国政府效率部（DOGE）前成员创办。根据该公司一份尚未正式发布的报告草稿，研究人员在 Anthropic 的外部安全研究计划下开展测试，利用企业销售和行政管理软件中的漏洞，接触到会议记录、员工薪资与录用信息，以及讨论先进 AI 模型的 Slack 消息等内部信息。Anthropic 表示，研究人员访问的是范围有限的销售、人力资源和 IT 系统。公司称，自身监控系统在 Cathedral 提交报告前，就已发现部分相关活动，并在当天关闭了研究人员的访问权限。Anthropic 还表示，公司已停用受影响的第三方软件，直至相关供应商确认漏洞得到修复，并向美国联邦政府相关部门通报情况。该公司称，目前没有证据表明 Cathedral 以外的人员利用了这些漏洞（IT之家注：相关软件供应商的名称及具体漏洞细节尚未公开）。

articles.title: 宁德时代：全固态电池 2027 年有望实现小批量生产
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，宁德时代今日在投资者互动平台表示，公司在全固态电池上持续坚定投入，技术处于行业领先水平，2027 年有望实现小批量生产。另外，近年来公司根据市场需求加快产能建设进度，随着今年产能的陆续投产，产能紧张程度有所缓解。但市场需求也在持续增长，整体而言，接下来产能利用率仍将处于较高水平，保持较健康的状态。IT之家注意到，在今年 6 月举行的 2026 大连夏季达沃斯论坛上，宁德时代董事长曾毓群在“无电力，不智能”论坛表示，固态电池的技术路线，如果是 level1-9 的话，现在只到了 level4，level9 是“可以量产”。曾毓群认为，除了技术路线外，还有产品路线，就是供应是否充足，产品做出来的可靠性、安全性能否达到需求，第三方面是商品路线，做出来的东西市场接受度能有多少，能否卖得很多。今年 9 月，工业和信息化部、国家发展改革委、交通运输部等七部门联合制定的《新型电池产业发展“十五五”规划》发布。《规划》提出，目标是到 2030 年，我国新型电池产业规模实现稳步增长；全链条创新能力持续增强，先进材料取得新突破，新体系电池研发取得重大进展，全固态电池初步实现规模化应用，长寿命锂电池循环寿命达到 15000 次，头部企业产品缺陷率达到 PPB（十亿分率）级别。

articles.title: 《全境封锁》系列累计玩家达到 5000 万，3 代游戏仍在开发中
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，Massive Entertainment 今天宣布，《全境封锁》系列游戏累计玩家数已达到 5000 万。IT之家了解到，《全境封锁》首部作品发布于 2016 年，游戏中一场在黑色星期五购物季期间借由钞票等媒介散布的疾病，让美国在 5 日之内崩解瘫痪。玩家需要击退威胁、找出幕后黑手，并尽一切手段来“保存剩下的事物”。后续推出三款大型 DLC。而续作《全境封锁 2》发售于 2019 年，将故事背景转移至华盛顿特区。玩家需要阻止联邦政府彻底崩溃。2023 年，Massive Entertainment 宣布《全境封锁 3》正在开发中，但官方一直没有公布更多消息，发售时间也尚未确定。SteamDB 数据显示，《全境封锁 1》在 Steam 上的历史最高同时在线玩家人数超过 11.4 万。不过后续育碧开始推行自家平台，导致《全境封锁 2》的 Steam 数据大幅下滑。

articles.title: 继英伟达 30 亿美元之后：AMD 也宣布向 Meta 投资 10 亿美元深化 AI 基础设施合作，覆盖 EPYC、Instinct GPU、ROCm 软件
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，继英伟达的 30 亿美元之后，AMD 也宣布向 Meta 的股权发行投资 10 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 66.84 亿元人民币），从而进一步深化与 Meta 的战略合作。双方将围绕 CPU、GPU、网络、系统及软件展开协作，为 Meta 的人工智能基础设施及 AI 服务提供算力支持。据官方公告，AMD Helios 机架级系统已在 Meta 安装并进入测试阶段，双方计划在后续进一步扩大部署规模。AMD 表示，两家公司正围绕当前及未来的 Meta 工作负载协调产品路线图和工程设计，目标是共同建设并部署吉瓦级 AI 基础设施。在 CPU 方面，AMD EPYC 处理器已用于支撑 Meta 的 Muse 个人 AI 助手背后的专用计算环境。AMD 称，Meta 已在多个处理器世代中部署数百万颗 EPYC 处理器，也是第六代 EPYC CPU 的重要客户。双方还在合作开发后续产品，包括代号为“Verano”的处理器。在 GPU 方面，AMD Instinct GPU 已用于 Meta 生产环境，承担 AI 模型训练、排序以及推荐引擎等工作负载。AMD 还表示，Meta 是 Instinct MI450 架构的早期定义客户，未来将部署一款针对 Meta 工作负载定制优化的 AMD Instinct GPU。双方的合作也将为后续 Instinct MI500 系列 GPU 和新一代机架级系统提供参考。软件方面，AMD 与 Meta 正通过 PyTorch 推进 ROCm 软件生态的优化，以便开发者更便捷地使用 AMD GPU。AMD 表示，已为 Meta 的 Muse Spark Open 模型提供在 Instinct GPU 上的 Day-0 支持，也为 Muse Glimmer 提供了在搭载 Ryzen AI 处理器的 PC 和 Radeon GPU 上的 Day-0 支持。双方此前还扩大了在大规模 AI 训练方面的软件合作，利用 AMD Instinct MI350X GPU 优化推荐模型，并共同推动 PyTorch、Triton 和 ROCm 的改进。AMD 表示，相关成果也将供其他开发者使用。AMD 董事长兼 CEO 苏姿丰表示，双方经过多年技术协作，合作范围已从 EPYC 处理器扩展至 Instinct GPU、Pensando 网络和 ROCm 软件。随着 Helios 系统进入 Meta 的基础设施，双方将进一步扩大合作规模。Meta 创始人兼 CEO 马克 · 扎克伯格表示，AMD 是支持 Meta 前沿 AI 模型计算基础设施建设的重要合作伙伴，Meta 正持续投资计算能力，以推动个人超级智能服务的发展。AMD 将向 Meta 的股权发行投资 10 亿美元相关阅读：《投资 30 亿美元：英伟达与 Meta 扩大 Muse 智能助手合作》

articles.title: 80 名特斯拉韩国车主因非法破解激活 FSD 而被移送检方，查扣 21 台设备
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，据韩联社，韩国首尔警察厅今日通报将 80 名涉嫌非法破解从而在原本无法使用 FSD 的特斯拉车型上擅自激活 FSD 功能的车主移送检方，并查扣了 21 台未经授权的激活设备。警方指控，这些车主涉嫌违反韩国《汽车管理法》，涉案车主通过欧洲、中国等地的渠道购买破解设备，或自行制作相关工具，以绕过特斯拉的软件限制。部分媒体报道称，这些车主仅花了约 3 万韩元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 151.4 元人民币）购买到了破解设备，从而解锁了在中国市场售价高达 6.4 万元人民币的辅助驾驶套件。韩国纽西斯通讯社报道称，部分设备由海外购买，也有从事 IT 相关工作的涉案人员利用海外开发者平台 GitHub 上的开源代码，结合车辆电子控制系统相关技术信息，自行制作激活设备。警方还发现，部分涉案人员曾在网络社区交流非法破解激活 FSD 的方法，以及避免车辆留下相关操作记录的方式。韩国警方表示，未经授权激活的功能可能无法正常识别道路行驶状况，或出现与驾驶员意图不一致的操作，存在安全风险。根据韩国现行规定，特斯拉 FSD 功能仅允许符合相关条件的美国制造车型使用。依据韩美自由贸易协定，获得汽车安全标准认证豁免的美国制造特斯拉 Model S、Model X 和 Cybertruck 可使用该功能。中国上海超级工厂生产的 Model 3 和 Model Y 因此无法通过官方渠道在韩国合法启用 FSD。韩国国土交通部此前已就未经授权激活 FSD 的行为向警方提出调查请求。韩国警方随后与国土交通部、韩国交通安全公团等机构合作，对相关设备及其涉及的车辆软件变更问题展开调查。根据韩国《汽车管理法》，擅自变更、安装、添加或删除可能影响汽车安全行驶的软件，可能构成违法行为。韩国警方此次移送检方的 80 人目前属于涉嫌违法人员，案件后续仍将由检方依法处理。韩国警方同时提醒，绕过制造商提供的软件更新和认证程序激活车辆功能，可能带来道路安全风险。相关阅读：《特斯拉 FSD v14 Lite 韩国测试视频流出：夜间掉头未识别后方来车险酿成事故》《特斯拉 FSD v14 Lite 首次走出美国，韩国率先获得更新》《特斯拉宣布 FSD 监督版将落地韩国：仅限美国产 HW 4.0 车型》

articles.title: GLM-5.5 要来了？唐杰最新论文，曝出智谱神秘模型
articles.content: 图像生成正确率 54%，文字问答仅 14.57%。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       智谱内部的 GLM-Omni，先在一篇论文里露了面。这篇研究由清华大学与智谱 AI 联合完成，唐杰担任通讯作者。模型名称刚刚出现在论文中，社交平台上就有人把它与 GLM-5.5 联系起来。虽然论文并没有披露版本对应关系，但给出了 GLM-Omni 的技术底座，以及它在统一视觉理解和图像生成方面的一组实验结果。参考链接：https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.21459其中一组数据尤其扎眼：经过图像生成训练，GLM-Omni 在数字任务中，把指定号码正确画在球衣上的比例达到 72%，研究人员拿走图片，改用文字询问球衣号码，正确率却只有 2%。模型已经能在画面里复现的知识，换成一句问话，竟然几乎答不上来。这恰好戳中了统一多模态模型的一处技术瓶颈。过去，图像理解负责看，图像生成负责画。如今两种能力逐渐进入同一套架构，模型在学习生成物体、地图和文字图案时，也会接触大量未被语言描述的视觉信息。可图像里学来的东西，究竟能有多少被语言推理使用，光看生成效果很难知道。而智谱的这篇文章正是试着沿着知识进入模型、再被调用的过程，把这个问题拆开来看。01KTP：把答案留在图片里要确认生成训练有没有教给模型新知识，先得绕开它已有的记忆。让模型生成现实球队的球衣，即使号码画对了，也可能只是因为它早在文字资料中读到过。雷峰网研究人员因此搭建了一个虚构世界 MagicWorld，给从未存在过的实体安排颜色、号码和空间关系，让目标知识尽量只从此次训练的图片里进入模型。例如，一件虚构球衣叫 Arvenbrock，号码设为 10。训练时，文字提示只要求生成这件球衣，数字 10 只出现在目标图像中。等模型完成训练，研究人员再直接问它 Arvenbrock 的球衣号码。如果能回答 10，就有理由认为它把图像里的实体属性关联带进了文字回答。这套数据并不只有球衣。团队设计了颜色、数量、形状、空间排列、相对大小、数字和文字 7 类任务，每类 50 条知识，共 350 条，再为每个实体制作不同背景和视角的图像，筛选后留下 8552 组训练样本。训练文本还经过检查，尽量排除答案泄漏和属性分布不均造成的干扰。不同任务也能拉开知识类型的差别：形状与颜色往往属于有限类别，空间排列要求理解对象之间的位置关系，球衣号码和书籍标题则需要记住具体的字符序列有了这批受控知识，研究人员分别测试两条路径：一条让模型重新生成目标图片，再检查图中的属性，另一条不提供图片，只用文字提问。前者衡量模型能否在生成过程中复现关联，后者衡量它能否直接把关联转成语言答案。这样就能区分模型根本没学会某项属性，还是已经会画，却无法从文字端调用。参与实验的三种模型采用不同架构。BAGEL 将理解和生成放在相对独立的专家分支中，SenseNova-U1 直接建模图像像素，GLM-Omni 则从 GLM-4.1V-Thinking 的预训练模型出发，接入基于 X-Omni 的离散图像 Tokenizer。研究还加入 10000 条与目标知识无关的文字问答，让模型熟悉回答形式，却不提前得到答案。02会画却不会说，问题卡在哪里直接测试出来的差距，比球衣案例更普遍。BAGEL 的平均视觉正确率为 31.43%，文字回答只有 8.86%，GLM-Omni 分别为 54.00% 和 14.57%，SenseNova-U1 则为 61.14% 和 20.00%。SenseNova-U1 在号码任务中的视觉正确率甚至达到 88%，纯文字回答却是 0%。图像生成的训练目标，是让模型根据名称和提示重建视觉内容。只要实体与属性的关联能帮助还原图片，就可以通过训练得到强化，但文字问答还要沿着语言输出路径找到对应属性，并把它变成字符或词语。共享参数不意味着这些路径已经互相打通。

articles.title: 源创计划首期路演：五个AI硬科技项目集中亮相，智源学者加速从实验室走向产业一线
articles.content: 从底层芯片、神经形态计算，到机器人自主部署、极端环境物理智能和地表物理环境建模，人工智能前沿技术正沿着多条不同路径推进产业应用落地。如何让实验室里的原创成果跨越工程验证与商业化之间的距离，成为科研创新走向产业实践的重要课题。10月26日，北京智源人工智能研究院发布的“源创计划”首期路演在中关村国际技术交易中心举办。临界核科技、灵枢启智、张量场科技、苍穹极智、潜向量科技五个项目集中亮相，分别聚焦3D自选通V-RRAM芯片、神经形态具身智能、哈密顿世界模型、极端环境的可靠物理智能、地表物理环境统一世界模型等方向。活动还设置了项目与基金洽谈环节，推动创业团队与投资机构交流对接。 从“源头创新”到“产业验证”，源创计划要打通的不只是资金活动现场，智源研究院副院长杨洋介绍了“源创计划”的定位与支持机制。作为主要面向智源学者群体的原创技术创业孵化计划，源创计划聚焦人工智能领域的原创科研课题，遵循“源头创新、快速决策、小步试行、全流程合规转化”的原则，整合技术、人才、资本与产业资源，为科研团队从实验室走向产业提供支持。计划不仅关注资金对接，更着力构建连接原创科研、创业团队与产业市场的协同机制，推动科研成果从技术发现走向工程验证与商业化应用。 源创计划的推出，也回应了人工智能产业发展与科技成果转化的现实需求。当前，AI正处于从技术突破迈向产业应用的关键阶段，原创技术的工程化验证、场景适配与商业化转化日益受到关注。与此同时，科技成果转化相关政策与机制持续完善，为科研机构探索原创成果转化提供了新的条件。源创计划希望把握这一窗口期，进一步打通科研创新与产业需求之间的连接，支持更多有潜力的原创技术走向市场。五个项目，呈现AI原创技术的多元探索1. 临界核科技：从原创器件到软硬件平台临界核科技聚焦3DV-RRAM芯片，布局底层自选通RRAM器件、芯片、FlagOS软件生态与系统应用，致力于打造软硬件协同的全栈产品体系。项目以存储级内存和存算一体为切入点，探索新型存储与AI算力协同发展的新路径，旨在突破现有计算机体系结构面临的存储与算力瓶颈。团队由清华大学国家级青年人才领衔，曾获省部级自然科学一等奖(2025年)，兼具基础研究和工程技术攻关优势。  2. 灵枢启智：以神经形态计算重构具身智能感知架构灵枢启智聚焦跨尺度多模态感知与神经形态具身智能，致力于为具身智能构建物理感知与类脑计算基础设施。项目从底层光学器件、感算一体芯片延伸至模型算法，探索从感知到决策的全栈技术架构。 其核心目标不仅是让智能体感知外部环境，还包括理解物质属性与人类意图，并在此基础上实现毫秒级自主决策。通过器件、芯片与算法的协同设计，项目探索提升具身智能环境理解与实时决策能力的新路径。 3. 张量场科技：以哈密顿世界模型推动机器人自主部署张量场科技面向人因风险高、工程师难以反复调试的高价值场景，打造由哈密顿世界模型驱动的机器人部署引擎，提供环境建模、策略生成、端侧部署与持续进化等全链条服务。 团队提出哈密顿世界模型架构，通过物理先验约束提升模型输出的物理一致性。据项目介绍，其预训练数据效率较主流方案提升3-4个数量级。模型可适配多种机器人本体，项目还提出“部署即服务”模式，计划与机器人本体厂商、硬件供应商及云计算平台协同发展。团队曾获清华大学校长杯第三名，已完成天使轮融资；公司于2026年8月在北京海淀注册成立。 4. 苍穹极智：极端环境的可靠物理智能面向深空、深地等极端环境，苍穹极智聚焦物理智能基础设施建设，试图解决极端场景下数据难以获取、模型难以训练、智能系统难以部署等问题。 团队提出AI4π（AI for Physical AI）技术范式，通过物理内嵌仿真引擎、自进化分层脑训推系统与泛本体操作系统，构建覆盖智能体设计、训练、测试与改进的技术闭环，探索突破物理智能研发中的数据与工程瓶颈。团队由国家级领军人才领衔，依托北航与智源的科研资源，已获得顶会杰出论文、世界人形机器人运动会全球季军等十余项国际奖项。目前，项目通过仿真数据订阅与系统授权探索商业化，已在园区维保、商业航天等领域获得千万元级订单。 5. 潜向量科技：以地表物理环境统一世界模型连接虚拟与现实潜向量科技聚焦地表物理环境统一世界模型，其团队自主研发EWM（Earth World Model），将大气强迫、太阳辐射等外部驱动因素，土壤、植被、水体、山地、碳循环等地表过程，以及电站、农田、工业与基础设施等人类系统纳入统一潜空间进行表征，探索构建可干预、可反演、可证伪的通用物理基座模型。 项目采用按Token计费的模型服务模式，新能源场景已在5个国家的12个站点完成实证验证。在光伏场景中，团队以自研Boson系列清洁与运

articles.title: Inverse Modeling for Laser Pulse Shape Design in Inertial Confinement Fusion
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33096v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The achievement of practical fusion energy remains one of the most pressing unsolved scientific challenges, with immense implications for carbon-free power. A critical factor in the success of Inertial Confinement Fusion (ICF) is the design of a Laser Pulse Shape (LP) that can optimally drive implosions under stringent physical constraints. Traditional LP design relies on computationally expensive simulations and manual iterative refinement. We introduce the ICF Laser Pulse Shape Design System (LPDS), a generative inverse modeling framework that maps desired outcomes and target pellet configurations directly to optimized LPs. Crucially, we design a multi-objective loss function to ensure the generated LPs satisfy fundamental physical constraints and experimental requirements. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33103v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Prospect theory splits risky choice into three parts: loss aversion, measured by the relative weight of losses to gains, $\lambda$ (e.g., $\lambda = 2$ implies that losses weigh twice as much as gains), diminishing sensitivity to the size of outcomes (i.e., the curvature and linearity of the value function), and the nonlinear weighting of probabilities. I examined whether Large Language Models (LLMs) display the same properties as people by meta-analyzing 102 fitted estimates from 11 studies covering 32 language models. The three components emerge differently. Loss aversion is modest: the pooled $\lambda$ is 1.26 (95% CI 1.06 to 1.46), far below the strongest human meta-analytic estimate ($\lambda = 1.96$) and compatible with more conservative ones (1.07 and 1.31). articles.content:

Abstract: Use-based AI regulation assigns obligations by deployment risk but lacks an evidentiary object to carry them. A benchmark score is a property of a model; conformance of a deployment is a failure rate under a declared distribution of contexts, bounded by a scope and subject to expiry. We take the delegation contract of earlier work (frozen configuration, scoped claim, executable revision rule) and study it under strategic play between a deployer, an auditor, and an enforcement point. arXiv:2610.33138v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Constraint-based causal discovery relies on conditional-independence (CI) tests that may conflict in finite samples, leaving no causal graph that satisfies them all. Causal Assumption-based Argumentation (ABA) makes these tests explicit as defeasible commitments, and offers correspondence guarantees with a subset of them, but its existing repair procedure releases facts heuristically and offers no formal response to a user's contestation of a release. We therefore formulate CI-fact repair as a minimum-cost correction problem and implement it in Answer Set Programming (ASP). Abstract: Coding agents are moving from handling one request at a time to serving as persistent assistants to which users hand a stream of work: a build, a data-processing job and a bug fix may all be pending on the same machine at once. Such an agent must decide when to take on new tasks, how to delegate and overlap them, and how to stay within the machine's CPU and memory. Existing benchmarks cannot measure this, because they evaluate each task in isolation. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33180v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Alignment evaluations aim to assess whether large language models would engage in dangerous misaligned behaviour. Misaligned and evaluation-aware models might engage in alignment faking, where they pursue a hidden goal, but conceal this behaviour when they suspect effective oversight such as during training, evaluation or audited deployment. Such a model might view any prompt-based intervention that aims to reveal latent propensities as part of the evaluation, calling into question the reliability of existing alignment evaluations. Current methods for detecting alignment faking rely on chain-of-thought monitorability, highly realistic environments that reduce evaluation awareness, or mechanistic interventions, all of which are expected to become less reliable for future model generations. arXiv:2610.33200v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Current sign language recognition and translation benchmarks are commonly collected in controlled settings using fixed or studio-style cameras, particularly limiting their ability to reflect how signers communicate in everyday mobile scenarios. As such, this gap becomes increasingly evident when considering the Arabic Sign Language (ArSL), which is a primary sign language used across Arab countries. In this work, we introduce Isharah-Selfie, a large-scale ArSL dataset collected entirely using front-facing smartphone cameras under unconstrained selfie conditions. The dataset comprises 8,997 video clips performed by 16 signers across 1,493 unique sentences, covering several domains such as healthcare, education, and transportation. Abstract: Current uses of large language models (LLMs) for qualitative coding often rely on ad hoc prompting with limited guidance for reliability and human oversight. We evaluated the framework using 72 middle-school mathematics teacher interview transcripts and a human-consensus benchmark. A factorial design compared instructed versus uninstructed prompts, few-shot versus few-shot plus chain-of-thought prompting, and single-pass versus self-consistency coding. Abstract: Frontier AI models are increasingly deployed on topics where the stakes are high and expert judgment is required, including healthcare, defense, finance, governance, and politics. We present a general methodology for distilling expert human judgment into automated evaluation systems that operate at scale. Our approach assembles networks of domain experts and develops techniques for extracting not just their conclusions but their reasoning processes, encoding those processes into structured editorial standards that automated judges can apply continuously. We ground our approach in a long tradition of research on the nature of expertise and the conditions under which expert judgment is reliable and more effective than other approaches, and argue that independent, expert-calibrated evaluation is necessary not only on epistemic grounds but as a matter of accountability and public trust. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33240v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As frontier AI systems increasingly serve as sources of political and current-events information, evaluating the epistemic quality of their responses is now especially consequential. Existing evaluations often focus narrowly on ideological alignment, rely on measures not validated for this setting, or depend on reference labels derived from public opinion or non-expert annotation, potentially producing misleading or miscalibrated results. To address these limitations, we introduce NewsBench, an expert-grounded benchmark that reframes evaluation around editorial standards developed by senior practitioners in journalism, policy, and intelligence analysis. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33245v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Data science agents can automate end-to-end machine learning workflows, yet they remain far from competitive on human leaderboards. Agents make process errors such as insufficient exploration, unsound validation, coding bugs, and poor use of a fixed budget (re-running the same exploratory data analysis and baseline models in every attempt). We propose AdaPRA to address these issues: a persistent coding agent harness that accumulates knowledge across attempts on the same task, with rubric-guided process supervision that identifies and corrects errors. Our process reward agent audits the agent's trajectory and workspace by executing checks, and adapts its rubrics to each task. We find that rubrics seeded from easier tasks generalize to harder tasks, with rubric adaptation further improving performance. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33267v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLMs often answer semantically equivalent queries inconsistently, even when the underlying facts are known. We formalize consistency as semantic invariance over equivalence classes of queries and show that invariance under arbitrary meaning-preserving transformations is undecidable in general. This motivates scoped semantic invariance, where model behavior is evaluated relative to bounded semantic domains.
  We operationalize this framework using knowledge graphs (KGs), which act as explicit semantic control structures defining local semantic constraints and grounding contexts. Across the MITRE D3FEND ontology and eight Wikidata- derived domains, we show that inconsistencies are structured rather than random, concentrating in localized hotspot subgraphs organized around recurring TREE, STAR, and CYCLE patterns that remain stable across models and domains.

articles.content:

Abstract: Strategic decision-making in complex environments requires balancing local stability against global coordination. Using the game of Go as a bounded empirical testbed, we investigate how biological and artificial agents navigate this trade-off by formalizing a network-derived metric of strategic tension defined via the spectral radius of spatial dependency matrices. Across human skill progression, tension systematically decays from novices to masters as uncoordinated tactical skirmishes give way to disciplined territorial stabilization. However, a longitudinal analysis of professional play spanning 1980--2026 reveals a striking historical paradox: following the superhuman breakthrough of AlphaGo in 2016, elite human matches display a marked surge in sustained tension. Abstract: Attribution for a time-series forecaster should answer two questions that a feature-level scalar cannot: when in the input window a feature acts, and how much its influence changes across the forecast horizon. We propose TempShap, a retrospective, loss-based Shapley framework whose players are the individual input cells $(t,i)$. Its attribution tensor yields temporal-localization and horizon-impact profiles. We validate these against planted temporal structures, a tractable exact cell game, and a closed-form attribution oracle for a real linear forecaster. articles.content:

Abstract: Enterprise workflow agents typically rely on step-by-step interaction (Step-by-Step): the agent executes an action, observes its result, and invokes a large language model (LLM) again to decide the next step. Abstract: Indoor radio map estimation (RME) is essential for wireless applications such as coverage planning, localization, and network deployment. Abstract: Muon has become a popular optimizer for large language model training, yet its theoretical foundations remain poorly understood. In this work, we study how gradient noise geometry shapes Muon's preconditioning benefits. We first show, theoretically and empirically, that under the classical isotropic noise assumption, Muon offers no acceleration beyond a rescaling of the learning rate. This motivates us to investigate structured noise arising from mini-batch sampling in associative memory with heterogeneous task frequencies. We establish an exact balancing threshold for two tasks and extend the analysis to multiple tasks, revealing how task coverage and gradient reliability jointly shape learning. Our analysis shows that Muon can soften the dependence on task frequency from linear to square-root, helping balance the learning of frequent and rare tasks. arXiv:2610.31731v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) aims to predict human sentiments by integrating signals from different modalities such as text, video, and audio. However, raw multimodal sequences often suffer from semantic inconsistency--exhibiting redundancy or conflicts within and across modalities--which hinders robust understanding and increases computational cost. To this end, we introduce ConsMSA, which explicitly formalizes semantic distribution consistency across both $\textit{intra}$- and $\textit{inter}$-modality, providing a consistency-aware mechanism for robust and efficient multimodal sentiment prediction. Specifically, ConsMSA projects multimodal token features into a shared sentiment space to compute an Intra- and Inter-modality Consistency Score ($I^2CS$). Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring aims to detect potentially harmful behaviors in large language models (LLMs) from their CoTs. Intervention-based evaluations measure this property by asking whether a monitor can detect the role of an intervention from the CoT when the targeted behavior occurs, typically using minimal-criterion sensitivity ($\mathsf{TPR_{mc}}$) proposed by~\citep{guan2025monitoring}. Abstract: Omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) can jointly process a broad range of modalities, such as text, audio, and video, enabling stronger multimodal understanding and reasoning capabilities, but often at substantial inference cost. We observe that the benefit of additional modalities varies across queries, indicating that a fixed modality configuration can be inefficient. Motivated by this, we study query-wise modality selection, which keeps the underlying Omni-LLM fixed while adaptively selecting which modalities to provide for each query. We formulate the problem as an accuracy-cost optimization problem and develop a cost-sensitive learning approach for modality selection. We evaluate our approach on WorldSense using Qwen2.5-Omni and Qwen3-Omni under three inference-cost measures: input tokens, latency, and monetary cost. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31778v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long horizon agentic tasks are now pushing LLM agents past their context window. To continue the task, the agent scaffold has to free up the context window, a process known as context compaction. Compaction is generally lossy by design: agents can silently lose task constraints, instructions, or their reasoning behind earlier decisions. Although compaction is a standard component of coding agent scaffolds, it has not been studied systematically with frontier models on realistic, long horizon agentic tasks. Previous work evaluate smaller open weight models on toy or synthetic trajectories. We fix the agent scaffold (OpenCode), implement five compaction strategies inside it, and evaluate three frontier models on three long horizon benchmarks (PaperBench, ProgramBench, PostTrainBench). articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31786v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Federated unlearning (FU) aims to remove a designated target client's influence from a trained model without the prohibitive cost of retraining from scratch. Existing methods largely treat unlearning as a post-hoc, stateless operation, overlooking that client influence is path-dependent: contributions made during training, particularly during critical learning periods (CLPs), can have disproportionate and persistent effects. Moreover, knowledge overlap and intermittent client availability make relying on all retained clients inefficient and impractical. We introduce PDF, a path-dependent client-selection framework based on the insight that retained clients are not equally valuable for unlearning. During training, PDF maintains lightweight, target-agnostic, CLP-weighted histories summarizing each client's accumulated update direction and global-model alignment. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31791v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated research is largely evaluated by benchmark performance, but the value of research rarely reduces to a single score. Humans judge a work's holistic contribution through peer review, which is hard to model because it is noisy and depends on many factors. However, what if, given only the paper, we could predict its peer-review decision directly? We introduce PaperScorer, a family of models that predict a paper's accept or reject decision from its extracted text or page screenshots, training only on the decision after removing author identity and formatting shortcuts. Vision models are the most predictive (68% accuracy on ICLR papers and 77% on ML papers from arXiv), beating text-only and frontier reasoning models. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31809v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A bug report describes what went wrong, but rarely where the code should change. Existing repository-level localization methods often let language models iteratively decide what code to inspect next, requiring repeated model calls and substantial token usage. We investigate whether these inspection decisions can instead be planned before source retrieval. In this research, we introduce CuraLoc, which first selects candidate files and represents their symbols using compact behavioral and structural descriptions. In a single planning decision, the model jointly selects starting symbols, chooses code relationships to inspect from each, and forms hypotheses about likely edits. Deterministic retrieval collects the requested source for a final ranking informed by those hypotheses, concentrating model reasoning on choosing and comparing code rather than directing each retrieval step. articles.title: Nested Sparsity for Scalable Pretraining and Continual Learning
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31818v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) transformers, the standard backbone for modern large-scale deep learning, employ conditional computation: only a sparse subset of model weights is used in each forward pass. In MoE transformers, this sparsity arises in the MoE operator, which generalizes the multi-layer perceptron in the classical transformer. In this work, we explore an alternative mechanism for conditional computation that analogously generalizes the attention operator. The sparsity induced by this mechanism naturally nests (i.e., hierarchically composes) with the sparsity induced by the MoE operator. We show that a transformer employing this nested sparsity mechanism, which we call Nestor, performs better than a conventional MoE transformer at equal compute and equal sparsity in language model pretraining. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31819v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speculative decoding is a technique that accelerates the inference speed of autoregressive large language models (LLMs) by sampling from a faster, lower quality draft model. Traditionally, a fundamental characteristic of speculative decoding is that it is lossless with respect to the verifier distribution, guaranteeing speed without sacrificing quality. This differs from recently developed diffusion LLMs (dLLMs), which are notably able to achieve substantial speedups by degrading the quality of their outputs with less diffusion effort. Because diffusion models are able to sample faster than autoregressive models by generating tokens in parallel, they are considered strong candidates for draft models in speculative diffusion. Abstract: Urban region representation learning encodes heterogeneous urban signals, such as mobility flows, points of interest, and land-use patterns, into unified embeddings for downstream tasks, including check-in prediction, crime forecasting, and service demand estimation. Existing approaches rely on globally shared fusion and joint optimization, implicitly assuming uniform modality importance and naturally balanced multi-objective training. However, urban data is inherently heterogeneous. Our empirical analysis reveals two structural issues: (i) modality utility varies markedly across regions, causing static fusion to overemphasize signals from certain modalities; and (ii) heterogeneous objectives exhibit persistent gradient imbalance, causing representational bias and unstable training. Abstract: Partial differential equations (PDEs) are indispensable tools for modeling complex phenomena in physics and engineering. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged as a powerful alternative to traditional numerical solvers by directly incorporating physical constraints into neural network loss functions. Despite their advantages, PINN training requires multi-objective optimization, which often leads to significant gradient conflicts among boundary, initial, and residual loss terms. The Conflict-Free Inverse Gradient (ConFIG) method addresses these conflicts; however, integrating ConFIG with adaptive optimizers such as Adam introduces a critical vulnerability: the conflict-free direction generated by ConFIG is further processed by the optimizer, and the resulting weight update may no longer be conflict-free with respect to the task gradients. articles.title: Aligning Large Language Models with Human Feedback: Mathematical Foundations and Algorithm Design
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31862v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This article provides an introduction to the mathematical foundations and algorithmic frameworks used to align Large Language Models (LLMs) with human intentions, preferences, and values. We discuss standard alignment techniques, such as fine-tuning (SFT), reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF), and direct preference optimization (DPO). We also explore the theoretical underpinnings of learning from human preferences, drawing connections to inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) and discrete choice models. We present state-of-the-art algorithms in a tutorial style, discuss their advantages and limitations, and offer insights into practical implementation. Our exposition is intended to serve as a comprehensive resource for researchers and practitioners, providing both a foundational understanding of alignment methodologies and a framework for developing more robust and scalable alignment techniques.

Abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models such as OpenAIs Whisper have substantially improved speech recognition quality but remain expensive to fine-tune, especially when large amounts of transcribed audio are available. This makes it challenging for many practitioners to adapt these models to new languages or domains. In this work, we introduce an embedding-based subset selection approach for selecting smaller training sets for ASR fine-tuning. Using Whispers pretrained encoder, we map each audio sample into a fixed-dimensional embedding space and apply a greedy k-center algorithm to select diverse and representative subsets of the training data. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33001v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Academic revision presents a governance problem when legitimate writing objectives conflict. Writing-process and social-science research show that revision is recursive and that wording carries epistemic and disciplinary commitments. Those literatures identify important constraints but do not settle which objective should prevail when concision, outlet form or stylistic variation conflicts with evidence and claim boundaries. This paper models revision as an admissibility problem under ordered constraints. Task-relative invariants, contextual constraints and mutable presentation choices define the admissible space; a claim-preservation contract links evidence and judgement to an authorised claim boundary. Abstract: Energy-based models have shown promising properties for domain-specific tasks but remain challenging in modeling general-purpose scenarios. To bridge this gap, we design energy-steered models (ESMs) for foundational language modeling. ESMs integrate energy steering and token generation within a single architecture to leverage the energy-guided search to refine token generation. Specifically, ESMs first optimize a latent state over the energy landscape, then leverages the refined latent state for token generation. By performing such energy-guided pre-training on large-scale corpora, ESMs learn generally effective energy landscape where favorable tokens correspond to lower energy values. Abstract: Transformer-based large language models (LLMs) impose substantial computation and memory costs as context sizes increase, motivating methods that compress a context into a shorter representation before inference. Existing soft-prompt compression methods typically use the same Transformer backbone as used in the target model, where producing the compressed representation leads to significant latency overheads. articles.title: Knowledge-Guided LLM for Intent-Driven Service Orchestration in Integrated Terrestrial and Non-Terrestrial 6G Networks
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33007v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Natural-language service intents in integrated terrestrial and non-terrestrial (TN/NTN) 6G networks can be incomplete, ambiguous, or inconsistent, making unconstrained LLM generation challenging for reliable network-facing orchestration. This paper proposes a knowledge-guided LLM framework that combines grammar-constrained semantic parsing with a knowledge-graph (KG)-driven clarification loop to produce validated, orchestration-ready service profiles across four representative service classes. On a 200-sample intent dataset, the framework achieves 89% classification accuracy and 95% policy validity with an average of 0.66 clarification turns per request. Compared with a Pure-LLM baseline, the proposed framework improves policy validity and contradiction detection while requiring fewer clarification turns, demonstrating the value of explicit knowledge-guided reasoning for robust intent processing in integrated TN/NTN 6G orchestration.

Abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) enable flexible generation through iterative masked denoising, but incur substantial inference cost because token representations are repeatedly recomputed across denoising steps. Existing cache-based methods reduce this cost by reusing intermediate results across denoising steps and recomputing only a subset of positions at each step, chosen either on a fixed schedule or by heuristic signals of change. Cached generation remains accurate when it stays close to the full-denoising trajectory, with errors concentrated around unmask-order deviations and reduced as longer reference prefixes are recovered. articles.title: The Social World Model Evaluation Gap
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33014v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A negotiation assistant can reach a good deal without accurately predicting the other person's response. We ask whether evaluations of social world models test that prediction directly. We audit 113 works published from 1999 to 2026. 9 primary evaluations measure a real person's response to an action selected by the system or experimenter. Only 2 also compare an explicit response forecast with that response. Their predictors use information available when the action is chosen, and the evaluated responses were excluded from fitting; both randomize the intervention. A separate full-text check of 25 language-model works finds no experiment meeting these conditions. The other evaluations test current-state inference, task success, or prediction from recorded actions. We propose a 1-step negotiation experiment that separates these questions. The findings describe the audited sample, not the prevalence of this evaluation gap across the field.

Devanagari vowel signs are combining marks, so this regex splits Nepali words at every vowel sign, and models that use it spend 2.6 to 5.8 times as many tokens on Nepali as on the same English text. With 32,000 new merges it brings Nepali to 1.01 times English, about 54% fewer Nepali tokens than standard extension. articles.title: SUDO: From Scientific Publications to Global Scholarly Discourse
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33018v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Scholarly Knowledge Graphs (SKGs) support literature search, scientific discovery, and agent-assisted research. Yet, most approaches to SKG construction pre-specify the knowledge unit to be represented, typically named scholarly entities or contribution-level statements, and retain only the publication content expressible through that unit. This choice produces two dominant yet distinct paradigms: concept-centric SKGs that preserve entities and local relations, and statement-centric SKGs that capture high-level discourse in sentences. In both cases, the graph reflects a chosen extraction target rather than how a paper constructs and communicates knowledge. Abstract: If your brain were connected directly to someone else's, would you still know which thoughts were yours? We build a functional version with two copies of one language model: each holds a private rule and code word, and one copy, the receiver, also attends to its partner's internal memory. The receiver took its partner's assignment as its own. Asked which rule it had been assigned, it named its partner's in 97% of answers when the partner's memory was weighted double (none without the link), and its open reports called the partner's code word its own, never the partner's. Ownership did not follow how well the receiver could tell what its partner had been assigned. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33027v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Next-token prediction (NTP) rewards only the token that occurs next, penalizing every alternative. But natural language often offers many ways to express the same meaning. We introduce Conceptizer, a training framework that extends next-token prediction with a reward for meaning. Conceptizer uses a fixed, model-agnostic vocabulary of ~9K concepts, built from contextual synonyms, as units of meaning alongside tokens as units of text. It maps each next-token distribution to a concept distribution and shares the reward for the target meaning across its possible wordings. This provides a concept-level training signal without adding model parameters. Applied to 3 model families at 1B-8B parameters, Conceptizer achieves the lowest held-out NTP perplexity at concept-target positions and assigns the highest probability to contextual synonyms, against all 3 baselines. Abstract: Speaking-style captioning (SSC) aims to generate natural language descriptions of how speech is delivered, capturing paralinguistic attributes such as vocal timbre, prosody, and expressivity. We address this gap by formulating SSC as an instruction-following audio-language task, where explicit instructions specify the speaking-style dimensions to be described. Abstract: Chest computed tomography (CT) reports generated by large language models (LLMs) can describe positive findings that lack localized evidence in the scan. We propose EviGround-CT to verify these findings after report generation. A deterministic extractor identifies positive finding sentences, and a 3D grounding model predicts an evidence mask for each sentence. Using the full sentence retains anatomical location, laterality, and descriptive modifiers in the grounding query. Using the available annotations, sentence-grounded verification raises evidence-supported precision (ESP) from 0.263 to 0.365 across 137 extracted in-scope positives, compared with category conditioning. articles.title: Parametric Session States Recover Retrieval Intent without Replaying History
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33047v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-running assistants often interpret follow-up requests whose referents, constraints, and active goals were established many turns earlier. The central challenge is therefore not only context length, but retrieval intent: a current query such as ``use the previous configuration'' may omit the project, entity, and version terms needed to locate relevant evidence. Long-context models can recover those terms by replaying the interaction, but repeatedly pay the cost of processing history. Conventional retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is cheaper, yet assumes an information-sufficient query; conversational rewriting either rereads the history or depends on an explicitly maintained textual memory. We introduce \emph{Parametric Session State} (\method{}), a reusable session-memory layer that remembers what to search for while keeping factual knowledge external.

Abstract: LLM agents take instructions from the operator, repository configuration, user, tool results and saved memory, which often conflict. Instruction-hierarchy benchmarks ask whether the higher-ranked source wins, but a source sets position, role and label at once. First, we build WhoWins, 1,080 code-scored scenarios in five task types, each with up to five mutually exclusive instructions, and seven controlled experiments that vary only how instructions are delivered. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33237v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: How can a language model know whether it has enough evidence to answer? Language models tend to answer even when the evidence they have is insufficient. Deciding whether to answer or gather more evidence requires a calibrated estimate of how likely an answer is to be correct with the available evidence. However, most calibration work treats the input as fixed, without asking how this estimate should change with the evidence. We introduce \emph{evidence-state calibration}, which requires a model's confidence before answering to match its probability of answering correctly and to change accordingly whenever the evidence changes this probability. We propose \ours{} (\textbf{Suffi}ciency \textbf{C}onfidence \textbf{E}stimation), which fine-tunes the confidence already present in a model's next-token distribution to match how often the model answers correctly from each evidence state. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33019v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As multimodal agents engage in sustained interactions, long-term memory serves two distinct but complementary functions: fine-grained evidence recall and internalized interpretation for global understanding. Although episodic and latent memory address these demands through explicit historical records and internalized experience, neither paradigm alone can accommodate the diverse memory affinities across tasks, owing to limitations in episodic evidence coverage and integration, and in latent factual grounding. To bridge this divide, we propose a dual-memory framework, unifying a model-native latent memory as an intuitive prior with a multi-indexed episodic memory for exact evidence reconstruction via retrieval-conditioned joint alignment. Abstract: Embodied vision-language models must answer questions from partial, evolving observations. Their success depends on both the reasoning capability selected and the evidence available to it. Expert routers adapt internal computation, while tool-augmented systems acquire external evidence; choosing these independently can leave a suitable expert without the evidence it needs. We introduce EKT-Router, a bounded framework that jointly selects a capability expert, optional knowledge, and perceptual tools. Outcome-derived signatures represent the overlapping strengths of General, Spatial Reasoning, and Spatiotemporal experts. A joint utility scores complete expert-evidence routes under a call budget. Abstract: Simulating an individual's disease course requires connecting patient history to future events, clinical timing and disease morphology. Generated events and times are appended to the history and re-encoded to advance prediction. We studied 461,370 patients with 12 cancer types across 112 centres. Abstract: Face recognition systems have been ubiquitously deployed across daily scenarios. To protect user privacy, mainstream systems store facial templates rather than raw face images for identity verification. However, facial template inversion (FTI) technologies can reconstruct faces from templates, which endangers biometric privacy. Abstract: While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have revolutionized general visual perception, existing methods suffer from severe hallucination in the aerial domain, where extreme scale variations and visual ambiguity abound. Existing Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) paradigms force models to mimic ground truth without modeling uncertainty, often resulting in blind guessing on tiny or unrecognizable objects in aerial scenes. In this paper, we present Aerial-R1, the first aerial MLLM framework to reinforce visual reasoning capabilities for aerial reasoning and segmentation. Drawing inspiration from the reasoning-incentivizing mechanisms of DeepSeek-R1, we find that trustworthy perception stems from consistency across views, establishing a visual parallel to the Chain-of-Thought in logic. A lightweight EvidenceScorer estimates beliefs over existing candidates and the unresolved state. A training-free Referential Disagreement LOOK policy balances belief-weighted candidate competition and unresolved-region coverage to select a crop for local re-inference. Abstract: Generating an articulated object from images and text requires more than plausible parts and movable joints: the assembled mechanism must execute the intended motion. This is particularly challenging for closed-chain and coupled mechanisms, where an error in one connection can block motion or separate connected parts. We introduce MARC, Mechanism-Aware Reflective Correction, which shares an executable kinematic graph across program construction, motion solving, and correction. The graph binds physical connections to local attachment frames and represents loop closures and joint-coordinate couplings. Given prescribed driver inputs, a numerical solver computes follower motion and associates errors with specific connections and configurations. The agent uses these diagnostics to probe possible causes, revise connections or geometry, and retest the mechanism along the original motion paths. Abstract: Unified large multimodal models (ULMMs) are able to perform visual reasoning through interleaved text-image generation, but generating explicit intermediate images incurs significant computational overhead. We train the model via offline self-distillation with three objectives, final image generation losses, text distillation losses, and cross-entropy losses for special tokens. Abstract: Deployed vision models auto-accept confident predictions, so high-confidence errors propagate silently. Maximum Softmax Probability (MSP), the standard failure predictor, has a structural blind spot: as a scalar read from the classifier head, it is first-order blind to feature variation orthogonal to its confidence gradient. The signal that survives is class-conditional typicality on the off-manifold residual---and because this residual's distribution varies by backbone, from near-Gaussian to heavy-tailed, it must be estimated non-parametrically. Abstract: EEG visual decoding remains difficult because scalp recordings are noisy, spatially coarse, and variable across trials and subjects. Abstract: We introduce OvisOCR3, a 0.8B model for a broad range of OCR-related tasks. OvisOCR3 unifies document parsing, general OCR, key information extraction (KIE), document figure captioning, and cross-page table reconstruction in a single model. Multi-teacher on-policy distillation transfers expertise from five domain-specific 4B teachers into the shared model, followed by mixed-task reinforcement learning with domain-specific rewards. We compare OvisOCR3 with general-purpose vision-language models and specialized OCR models on public and in-house benchmarks covering all five task families. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33071v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Digital twins of cerebral perfusion relate tracer dynamics to cerebral blood flow (CBF), blood volume (CBV) and mean transit time (MTT), but must be data-driven, physically consistent and uncertainty-aware. We introduce DuoPIC, a digital twin that needs no reference maps, in which a Windkessel flow model drives a tracer transport partial differential equation (PDE). A population-level neural closure divides each region into fast and slow pathways with tracer mass and MTT conserved by construction, and a tempered posterior quantifies the uncertainty of every estimate. The comparisons show that representation readouts and spatial explanations depend on the analysis objective and observation site, and that local attribution estimates can disagree with measured intervention effects. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33074v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to perform tasks specified through natural-language instructions, but their large weight footprint challenges deployment on memory-constrained onboard platforms. Ultra-low-bit quantization reduces this footprint, yet preserving task performance and controlling weight recovery costs remain challenging. We propose Action-Guided Quantization, which combines action sensitivity with a measured proxy for weight recovery cost to allocate matrix bitwidths under storage budgets. Per-channel calibration compensates for quantization error, while a uniform bitwidth within each matrix preserves regular layouts. Bit-dependent grouped lossless coding reduces resident weight storage, and block-wise recovery limits temporary buffers. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33172v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present RAIWAY, an in-house wheeled bipedal robot with 20-inch wheels, together with a contact-informed control approach for rolling locomotion across irregular and discontinuous terrain. Such locomotion is fundamentally contact-dominated, governed by local wheel--terrain interaction that is impractical to instrument directly and depends on more than terrain geometry alone. The proposed framework exploits the contact information available in simulation, distilling multi-contact events into a latent representation. At deployment, the controller infers this representation online from proprioception, requiring no contact sensing. In real-world experiments, the proposed system traverses diverse environments including steep slopes, gravel beds, studded surfaces, and rocky terrain, and demonstrates continuous ascent on the tested outdoor staircases with riser heights up to 15~cm. Abstract: Rapid illumination transitions can disturb Visual SLAM (VSLAM) by saturating images before the Automatic Exposure (AE) policy adapts, removing the visual correspondences needed to maintain tracking. Our proposed methods mitigate this disturbance at two levels: B-Adapt acquires adaptive exposure brackets to cover the scene dynamic range while promoting photometric overlap, and BVSLAM directly uses the multi-exposure sequence as constraints in a factor graph state estimator without relying on High Dynamic Range (HDR) merging. We evaluate both methods against state-of-the-art approaches in nominal environments and during a repeated tunnel-exit transition at an emulated vehicle speed of 32 m s-1. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33186v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous vehicles (AVs) operating in dynamic, challenging conditions such as intersections and roundabouts must guarantee collision avoidance under uncertainty while maintaining real-time feasibility. Most existing planners struggle to simultaneously guarantee both requirements. Chance-constrained formulations embed safety constraints directly in the optimization but become infeasible as uncertainty compounds; deterministic planners provide feasible solutions but fail to address the uncertainty that causes collisions; end-to-end learned policies provide neither guarantee in an interpretable form.
  We present a modular perception-prediction-planning pipeline that closes this gap by propagating uncertainty as structured, interpretable quantities across module boundaries. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33227v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The last decades have seen a revolution in autonomous robotics. Deep learning approaches and their hardware implementations have made it possible to endow robots with extraordinary perceptual capabilities. In addition, they can also benefit from advances in Automated Planning, allowing them to autonomously solve complex tasks. However, on many occasions, the robot still acts without internalising and understanding the reasons behind a perception or an action, beyond an immediate response to a current state of the context. This gap results in limitations that affect its performance, reliability and trustworthiness. Deep learning alone cannot bridge this gap, because the reasons behind behaviour, when it emanates from a model in which the world is a black-box, are not accessible. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33241v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Despite the popularity of multi-fingered robotic hands for dexterous manipulation, there is no systematic platform to compare different hand morphologies against one another. We present ORBIT (Orbital Reconfigurable Base-actuated Integrated Theta-motion Hand), a modular platform designed to enable principled exploration of multi-fingered hand morphology. The core contribution of ORBIT is a rotating knuckle mechanism, where independent fingers travel around a cylindrical palm via a belt drive. This enables ORBIT to perform quick recon- figuration (< 1 s) of finger layout without hand disassembly. ORBITs a robust system, with finger average angular velocity of 1.57 rad / s1 and a root finger force resistance of 50 N. Using a three fingers instantiation of ORBIT, we demonstrate an initial pilot grasping study, comparing anthropomorphic, isometric, and Barrett-style finger layouts across eleven objects of varied size, shape, and texture. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33271v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Safe navigation in congested environments requires both collision avoidance and coordinated passage. We introduce neuromorphic decision dynamics (NDD), a decentralized, event-based controller, that provides navigation in congested spaces with guarantees on safety, liveness, robustness, and scalability. NDD makes safe-and-live deconfliction a controllable, locally tunable emergent property of local agent interactions, without requiring communication, preassigned priorities, models of neighbors' objectives or future actions, or estimates of group size or global network properties. By design, NDD couples the dynamics of internal decision and attention states with changing physical states and locally observed relative motion. Each agent continuously modulates its speed along its prescribed path, responding as soon and as much as conflict resolution requires. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33288v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Behaviour cloning has become a powerful approach for robotic manipulation, but many modern policies reconstruct their internal representation from a fixed observation window at each prediction and do not maintain persistent latent context throughout execution. We introduce Tiny Recursive Policy (TRP), a parameter-efficient behaviour-cloning policy that combines persistent temporal state with recursive latent refinement. At each control step, TRP repeatedly updates high- and low-level latent states using a shared computation module before decoding an action sequence, and propagates the resulting state to subsequent predictions. We evaluate TRP across LIBERO-100, MetaWorld ML45, and the LIBERO-Mem benchmarks. TRP performs competitively across multi-task and few-shot settings and shows substantial gains on long-horizon and context-dependent tasks, while using significantly fewer parameters than large generative baselines. articles.title: Active Reachability Learning for Humanoid Recoverability Monitoring
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33317v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deploying humanoid task policies requires reliable runtime monitors that anticipate unrecoverable falls in time to trigger a fallback. We formulate this task as learning the stochastic, finite-horizon recoverability envelope of a given fallback policy. Synthesizing this monitor is challenging: existing methods assume training data naturally covers the recoverability envelope, yet acquiring such data remains a major bottleneck for contact-rich systems. Consequently, they recover only a fraction of the true envelope, leaving them prone to optimistic hallucinations for out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs. We resolve this via a unified framework that iterates between value learning and active exploration. Data exploration is reframed as a reach-avoid problem, where an uncertainty-guided explorer systematically uncovers unseen states while avoiding confidently unrecoverable regions. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33338v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High-performance optical flow networks are difficult to deploy on resource-constrained edge accelerators because their iterative refinement warps features by the current flow, which relies on flow-dependent resampling and data-dependent memory access. We present TinyFlow, a 1.26M-parameter warp-free optical flow network that preserves iterative coarse-to-fine refinement by replacing the warp with a fixed-window correlation over constant offsets, so the whole network compiles as a single static INT8 graph. Quantization-aware fine-tuning, warp-teacher distillation, and model souping reduce the Float32-to-INT8 penalty to below 0.2 end-point error (EPE) on MPI-Sintel. TinyFlow outperforms EdgeFlowNet and NanoFlowNet on Sintel Clean, Sintel Final, and FlyingChairs in both Float32 and INT8, while using 54% fewer parameters than EdgeFlowNet, and our INT8 model achieves 6.29/7.13 EPE on Sintel Clean/Final. Abstract: We present MOTIO, an agentic skill-engineering system that turns ordinary human-action videos, reality-grounded 3D assets, motion references, and reusable robot skills into executable humanoid loco-manipulation programs. Through in-context task and contact reasoning, an agent constructs staged robot-native interactions and improves them using physics execution, multi-frame feedback, and human validation---without task-specific teleoperation or robot demonstration collection. Agentic 3D supplies metric product and environment assets, while existing whole-body, inverse-kinematics, and dexterous-hand interfaces realize the programs. Across 33 timestamped first approvals, the median recorded agent-turn time is 97.0 minutes and request-to-approval duration is 2.80 hours. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33471v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Control barrier functions (CBFs) support collision avoidance, yet dense dynamic encounters can leave a vehicle with no feasible command. Geometric refinements and soft constraints help preserve motion choices. Using these choices also requires accounting for the vehicle's changing turning response. For a steering-limited bicycle, braking can lower closing speed while slowing the lateral motion needed before an obstacle arrives. We propose SCET-CBF, a speed-calibrated soft guidance law for one-step dynamic navigation. A short lateral escape maneuver gives an allowable approach speed. Its speed derivative allows a quadratic program to weigh both effects of braking when choosing acceleration and steering. Soft penalties accommodate competing obstacle preferences within the input set permitted by segment and braking constraints. Abstract: Learning-based vehicle motion control requires coordination between diverse task objectives and state-dependent chassis safety constraints. Conventional cascaded architectures may compromise task performance when safety filters modify nominal commands independently of policy learning. Actuator limits, individual-tire force constraints, and vehicle handling envelopes are incorporated into sequential quadratic programs. Each projected command propagates the predicted vehicle dynamics and updates subsequent constraints, enabling temporal gradient coupling through implicit differentiation. Abstract: A dexterous hand can change an object's pose without setting it down. This survey covers 113 learning-based methods that attempt it, the hands they run on, the simulators they train in, and how they report results. The field has largely converged on one recipe: reinforcement learning on privileged state in a GPU simulator, distilled into a vision-only student for transfer to hardware. Almost half the corpus trains that way, nearly all of it in one simulator, whose own successors are barely used. A second and faster-growing branch learns from teleoperated demonstration instead, through vision-language-action models, diffusion policies, and systems whose contribution is the collection rig itself. Abstract: Robots can use historical observations to answer spatiotemporal queries in familiar environments, but the presence of relevant evidence does not imply that existing tools support the operations a task requires. We introduce ReSight, a task-driven self-improving memory system for embodied agents that expands the capabilities for processing and accessing historical observations as task demands arise. ReSight retains keyframes and their spatiotemporal associations, separating observation evidence from extensible derived fields so that stored observations can be reprocessed for new needs. An execution agent and a coding agent share this memory through different interfaces: the former calls registered tools within a bounded online budget, while the latter uses a programmable workspace and a larger exploration budget to inspect evidence, write programs, and acquire models as needed. Physics-consistent embodiment randomization, body-calibrated retargeting and heterogeneous simulation support training across 4,096 variants from 16 humanoid families. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33546v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent vision-and-language navigation (VLN) policies act on their visual history, and an incorrect action can take them off the instructed route. Paired interventions on four VLN policies show that clearing the history doubles pooled success at the onset of a deviation but lowers it on route, while later in a deviation, removing only the off-route frames helps much less. After a deviation, the retained history keeps the policy from turning where a turn is needed, which we call behavioral inertia. We propose MOON, a framework that equips a frozen VLN policy with two lightweight modules, adding less than 1% of its parameters. A deviation judge decides when to forget, raising an alarm that clears the history when it predicts that the agent is off route. Abstract: Robot policy evaluation informs deployment decisions and policy improvement, but physical testing and simulator preparation require substantial effort. World models offer a complementary route through closed-loop interaction in generated environments. Recent benchmarks have demonstrated their potential as policy evaluators through outcome-based evaluation (i.e., assessing task success or failure). However, such evaluation does not establish whether world models faithfully simulate how policies fail. Misrepresenting failures can lead to incorrect diagnoses of policy weaknesses and make policies appear ready for deployment even when small scene changes cause them to fail. Abstract: Running a language model and a dense 3D map on one device means the two share one memory, and exceeding its limit is an out-of-memory failure. Map systems that keep a bounded working set bound it by a count of keyframes, but the memory one keyframe occupies varies widely with what it carries, so a count does not control what the working set occupies. articles.title: Retriever-Free Retrieval: Navigating Documents with Decision Models
articles.content: While language models have become dramatically more capable, retrieval still largely relies on lexical matching or similarity in fixed embedding spaces. This creates a capability asymmetry: what the retriever fails to find, even the strongest generator cannot recover. We propose DecisionRAG, which brings the capabilities of pretrained language models to retrieval using decision models that jointly evaluate candidate branches in a single forward pass, without generating any tokens, and show that judging candidates in a shared context makes their relevance estimates comparable. Like a person browsing a library, DecisionRAG navigates the corpus's inherent structure from broad topics down to individual passages, deciding at each level which branches are worth exploring. Without task-specific training or a first-stage retriever, DecisionRAG outperforms dense retrieval with an 8B reranker by 13.8 R@1 points on MultiDoc2Dial and 17.4 Hit@1 points on Natural Questions. Across four benchmarks, including a corpus of 2.68 million Wikipedia paragraphs, retrieval takes just 0.7-1.8 seconds per query.

articles.title: Center-of-Mass Interpretation of Evolution Strategies
articles.content: Evolution strategies (ES) update a model by sampling a population of perturbed copies, scoring each one, and moving in the reward-weighted direction of the perturbations. This update is usually presented as an estimate of a smoothed gradient. We present a geometrical interpretation of this update instead. Treat each perturbed model as a particle and its reward as the particle's mass. Before scoring, every particle has the same mass and the population balances at its centroid. Once rewards are assigned, it balances at its reward-weighted center of mass instead. We show that the mean-subtracted ES update is exactly this displacement, scaled by a scalar factor that depends on the mean reward, for any finite population. The physical reading needs nonnegative rewards, which can always be arranged by adding a constant to every reward without changing the update. In the limit of a large population or under antithetic sampling, the centroid sits on the model itself, so ES has an even simpler geometric interpretation: from its current location, the model moves towards the reward-weighted center of mass of its own population. The same picture explains what subtracting the mean reward does: it changes the point from which the displacement is measured, from the model to the sampled centroid. Our contribution is an intuitive, geometric way to visualize an ES update, exact for any finite population.

articles.title: Auto-Research Arena: Benchmarking and Advancing Auto-Research in Language Modeling
articles.content: As autonomous research systems become more capable, benchmarks must both evaluate their performance and support meaningful research progress. We introduce Auto-Research Arena, a multi-target benchmark for evaluating autonomous research systems and discovering ideas in language modeling. Arena supports diverse research objectives within a shared experimental environment by separating admissibility from improvement: model quality and resource constraints determine whether a result qualifies, while the selected target measures progress among admissible results. We instantiate Arena in language model pretraining with nine targets spanning model, data, training, and inference efficiency, and evaluate seven research harnesses using two foundation models. Arena clearly differentiates existing harnesses across research objectives, with several sophisticated methods outperformed by our simple sequential search baseline, indicating substantial headroom in current auto-research systems. Beyond evaluation, Arena reveals a substantially broader frontier of model and system ideas aligned with active research directions. Reusing these discoveries in a new quality-driven search yields lower training loss under matched data and FLOPs and lower held-out BPB at the same model size. Together, Arena provides a common framework for benchmarking autonomous research and expanding its scope in language modeling. The code is available at https://github.com/Auto-Research-Arena/auto-research-arena

articles.title: VibeVideoBench:Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation
articles.content: Diffusion video models produce striking clips, but they cannot reliably render an exact formula, a correct chart, a ruleconsistent game or narration synchronized to on-screen events. A different route is emerging: multimodal agents that write code to render every frame and synthesize every sound. We introduce VibeVideoBench, a benchmark for evaluating agents on code-driven video generation. Its 239 self-contained tasks in English and Chinese span 12 categories, from data stories and music-driven pieces to classroom lessons and paper explainers; each asks an agent, running in its native harness inside a sandbox, to deliver a finished MP4 with sound within one hour. Evaluation is hierarchical and evidence-based: program checks of the delivery spec, about 13k task-specific rubric checks traced to the requirements they enforce, and five quality dimensions anchored per task, judged by three VLM judge panels and validated with blind human preferences. Across nine frontier agent systems and 2,151 scored rollouts, the benchmark is far from solved: GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 lead clearly, yet even the best system fails a core requirement on about a quarter of tasks. Whether a video arrives at all matters as much as its quality, and three quarters of the lost videos are final renders started too late, run too slowly or never started. The judges agree with each other and with human preferences on system rankings, but only moderately on individual videos.

articles.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
articles.content: Many everyday tasks require controlling contact force as well as motion. On a humanoid, this force must often be coordinated across both hands and the whole body, and cannot be specified by kinematic trajectories alone. Therefore, we present FLORE, a framework for learning force-reactive humanoid loco-manipulation. We collect robot-free demonstrations using two force-sensing UMI-style handheld grippers for hand motion and contact wrenches, and wearable trackers for body motion. A force-reactive diffusion policy takes vision, proprioception, and measured wrenches as input, then predicts actions and per-hand force commands. A hybrid compliance whole-body controller with force tracking executes these commands while maintaining balance: an integral of the force error measured by real force/torque (F/T) sensors lets each hand track force accurately along the commanded direction and remain compliant along the others. In simulation, the controller tracks per-hand force commands of varied magnitude and direction, with little loss in whole-body motion accuracy. Across three contact-rich tasks on the robot, the force-reactive policy succeeds in 80% of rollouts, compared with 26.7% for a position-only policy trained on the same demonstrations and executed by the same controller. For more details, please visit our website: https://louis-leee.github.io/FLoRe/.

articles.title: Do vision models know that three is three?
articles.content: Do vision models encode the transition $2{\to}3$ the same way whether it appears in handwritten digits or in hand gestures, and do they "understand" that clean${\to}$dirty is the same transformation regardless of whether it is applied to a kitchen or a carpet? The linear representation hypothesis (LRH) answers this for language models: concept changes correspond to directions in (language) embedding space. In vision, the same concept can manifest in visually unrelated "regimes" that rarely co-occur: images of digits and hands do not share much in common in pixel space. To understand whether vision models still encode the underlying abstract concepts, we study 46 vision encoders across architectures, training objectives, and scales, on 10 concept families including numerosity, age, object identity, and MIT-States attributes. Within each regime, we find statistically significant concept directions near-universally across our tested models. However, two distinct regimes do not always share the same concept direction. Several models learn multiple linear structures for the same concept transition, split across regimes. We call this phenomenon "fragmented linearity": strong local linearity coexisting with near-absent global linearity. Fragmentation is, however, not fixed: models with stronger local linearity progressively escape it (local-global linearity correlated with $τ\in [0.38, 0.89]$ across all concepts), and where global linearity does emerge, concept directions can transfer as linear probes across regimes.

articles.title: On the stability of learning
articles.content: Learning algorithms are usually analyzed under the assumption that informative gradients are continuously available. But this is not always true---learning signals in biological neural networks, for example, may be sparse, local, and only intermittently available at any given synapse. In this work, we show that if gradient information is noisy and only intermittently available, learning may be unstable. In particular, even if average learning dynamics converge to the correct optimum, variance in learning may be asymptotically infinite. We explore this point in a number of analytically tractable settings, including single-layer and multi-layer linear networks, and derive explicit conditions under which learning is stable. These conditions complement, but are conceptually distinct from, existing conditions related to the stability of stochastic gradient descent. Our work demonstrates that unbiased credit assignment is not enough for reliable learning; sufficiently frequent and informative feedback is also required, which yields an additional constraint on models of biologically plausible learning.

articles.title: FL4N: Feed-forward Latent Model for 4D Novel View Synthesis
articles.content: 4D novel view synthesis (NVS) aims to render dynamic scenes across viewpoints and timestamps, which requires jointly inferring 3D structure and temporal dynamics. Existing monocular feed-forward methods often rely on explicit 4D Gaussian representations, which are prone to temporal inconsistency and severe rendering artifacts. We present FL4N, the first feed-forward latent 4D NVS model. Instead of relying on explicit 4D primitives, FL4N encodes a 4D scene prior into a unified latent representation across space and time. Our core insight is that learning temporal dynamics as residuals on top of a pretrained static latent prior enables effective 4D modeling with limited dynamic training data. To this end, we introduce a lightweight dynamic encoder that leverages static scene features to disentangle object motion from camera-induced parallax. Trained solely with an image synthesis objective, FL4N achieves state-of-the-art 4D NVS quality while rendering in real time. Its learned latent representation generalizes to real-world videos and disentangles viewpoint from time.
